digest.headline: US technology shares entered a correction after an artificial intelligence-led sell-off erased billions in market value.

lede.b: Technology stocks in the United States dropped sharply, pulling major stock indexes into a correction, which means a drop of ten percent or more from recent highs. Nvidia, a giant maker of computer chips, lost nearly nine hundred billion dollars in market value during this rout. A correction is a market drop that wipes out recent gains and makes investors nervous. At the same time, the price of copper fell, showing that factories and builders expect lower demand for materials. This drop in metal prices happened alongside the wider fall in stock prices. The Nasdaq index fell by ten percent across seven consecutive sessions of losses.
lede.i: US tech shares plunged into correction territory following an artificial intelligence-led rout that erased nearly $900bn from Nvidia alone. The Nasdaq dropped 10% across seven consecutive sessions of losses, dragging broader indices down with it. Industrial metal prices fell simultaneously as copper dropped sharply on softening manufacturing demand expectations. This industrial commodity sell-off reinforced the wider deflation of risk assets across American equity markets. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all retreated from record highs reached earlier in 2026.
lede.a: US equities entered correction territory as an AI-fuelled tech rout drove a severe repricing of valuations. Nvidia shed nearly $900bn in market value, dragging the Nasdaq down 10% across 7 consecutive sessions of losses and pulling the S&P 500 alongside the Dow off their record 2026 highs. Concurrently, copper prices plunged on weaker manufacturing demand expectations, compounding the broader equity correction. This industrial metal sell-off provided a negative macroeconomic signal that aligned with tightening risk sentiment across major US indices. The convergence of tech de-rating and industrial commodity weakness defined the session's price action.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US markets face tech sell-off and falling copper prices

stories.t: Nasdaq and Major Indices Enter Correction After AI-Fuelled Rout
stories.b: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all hit record highs earlier in 2026 before suffering an artificial intelligence-fuelled sell-off. The Nasdaq plunged 10% and neared a bear market during a fall spanning 7 straight sessions. Nvidia led the tech stock rout by shedding nearly $900bn in market value. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 both drove into correction territory.
stories.i: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq reached record highs in 2026 before an AI-fuelled sell-off triggered a severe deflation of tech valuations. The Nasdaq plunged 10% across 7 consecutive sessions of losses, pushing the index toward a bear market. Nvidia drove the tech stock rout by shedding nearly $900bn in market value, dragging both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 into correction territory.
stories.a: Record highs across the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq in 2026 preceded an AI-driven sell-off that forced the Nasdaq down 10% over 7 consecutive negative sessions. Nvidia shed nearly $900bn in market value, leading a tech rout that propelled the S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 into correction territory. The drawdown reflects compressed valuations following extreme concentration in artificial intelligence leaders.

stories.t: Copper Prices Plunge as Investors Monitor Wider Economic Signals
stories.b: Copper prices are plunging and sending a warning for the US economy. Industrial metals like copper are often watched to gauge overall economic health because they are used in many manufacturing sectors. The drop in copper coincides with a broader downward move in American equities.
stories.i: Copper prices are plunging, delivering a warning signal for the US economy. The drop in industrial metal prices reflects weakening demand expectations across manufacturing sectors. This commodity sell-off coincides with the wider correction hitting American equity indices.
stories.a: Plunging copper prices provide a negative growth signal for the broader US economy. Industrial metals pricing weakness correlates with deteriorating demand assumptions in cyclical sectors. This commodity liquidation occurs simultaneously with the equity market correction.

stories.a: UK headline inflation printed at a fresh 12-month high, testing rate trajectory assumptions. The compression in real household disposable income alters consumption velocity. Analysts must re-evaluate rate path pricing across short-dated money markets.

stories.i: Sterling broke past the 1.31 threshold against the US dollar. The exchange rate moved higher as broader dollar strength developed across global currency markets. Traders adjusted foreign exchange positions in response to the shift. The GBP/USD pair reflects these cross-border capital flows.

stories.t: Ruling Bloc Seeks Higher Defense Outlays
stories.b: Japan's ruling political group wants to spend lots of money on defense. They are asking for 70 trillion yen or even more. Money spent by the government on defense goes toward military protection. This is a very large funding target for the country.
stories.i: Japan's ruling bloc demands defense spending of 70 trillion yen or more. The coalition presses for this substantial budget expansion to bolster military capabilities. Officials set this high financial threshold for future security outlays.
stories.a: Japan's ruling bloc demands defense spending of 70 trillion yen or more. The fiscal expansion signals a permanent structural shift in national security funding. Bond markets now price the sovereign debt issuance required to back these long-term military procurement commitments.

stories.t: Tokyo Tax Authorities Uncover Unreported Crypto Income
stories.b: Tax workers in Tokyo looked into the accounts of people who own digital money. They found that 91 crypto holders did not report all their earnings. These people hid a total of $24.5 million in income. Crypto is virtual money stored on computers.
stories.i: Tokyo tax officials audit 91 crypto holders and uncover $24.5 million in unreported income. The municipal tax authority targets digital asset compliance to capture missed tax liabilities. Investigators expose widespread omissions in virtual currency reporting across the capital.
stories.a: Tokyo tax officials audit 91 crypto holders, uncovering $24.5 million in unreported income. The enforcement action demonstrates intensified scrutiny of decentralized asset transactions by domestic revenue agencies. Investigators utilize advanced blockchain tracing to identify systemic underreporting among high-net-worth digital asset investors.

politics.a: Japan's ruling bloc demands defense spending of 70 trillion yen or more, forcing the administration to reconcile fiscal consolidation goals with military expansion. stories.b: A big Saudi energy company named Saudi Aramco just signed a new installation works contract. Gas Arabian Services Co. is the company that will do the work. They agreed on a unit-rate contract price. Another company called Almar also reached a financial close for a project called Zuluf II. That deal is worth $940m.
stories.i: Gas Arabian Services Co. signed an installation works contract with Saudi Aramco. The agreement uses a unit-rate pricing structure. Separately, Almar reached a financial close for the Zuluf II project with Saudi Aramco. That financing totals $940m.

In a parallel transaction, Almar achieved financial close for the Zuluf II project tied to Aramco, securing $940m in capital. These commitments underscore the ongoing deployment of capital into upstream infrastructure despite broader macroeconomic headwinds.

stories.t: OPEC and Russia Discuss Output Cuts as Oil Prices Move
stories.b: Global oil prices went up because people hope for production cuts from countries outside of OPEC. OPEC and Russia talked about making a smooth global deal to cut oil production. OPEC stands for the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries. They met with South Sudanese ministers on a keynote stage.
stories.i: Oil prices extended gains due to expectations surrounding non-OPEC output cuts. OPEC and Russia indicated a smooth path toward a global agreement on lowering production. Representatives from OPEC also joined African Continental Free Trade Area and Dangote Refinery officials on the keynote stage at the South Sudan Oil & Power 2026 event.
stories.a: Crude futures extended gains as markets priced in prospective non-OPEC output cuts. OPEC and Russia signaled alignment regarding a global framework on production quotas. Concurrently, OPEC delegates appeared alongside representatives from the African Continental Free Trade Area and Dangote Refinery at the South Sudan Oil & Power 2026 conference.

stories.t: Climate Talks Stall at Cop31 Over Fossil Fuel Phaseout
stories.b: Climate talks at the Cop31 summit stopped making progress in Turkey. Countries could not agree on electrification and financial aid for the developing world. Some nations thought about forcing a showdown with Saudi Arabia and its allies. The argument is over the global need to phase out fossil fuels.
stories.i: Negotiations at the Cop31 summit reached a standstill in Turkey. Participating nations failed to reach consensus on electrification and climate finance for developing countries. Several delegations subsequently considered challenging Saudi Arabia and its allies regarding the phaseout of fossil fuels.
stories.a: The Cop31 summit in Turkey hit an impasse after delegates failed to secure agreement on electrification and development finance frameworks. This deadlock has prompted certain member states to weigh a direct confrontation with Saudi Arabia and aligned nations regarding language on phasing out fossil fuels.
